# Cloud Commands

Every command the `cloud` module offers, from its declarations, in order of the resource each acts on. Each command's help says the same.

## `lnk cloud connect`

Connect an AWS or Google Cloud account, for buckets and boxes

```usage
lnk cloud connect <kind> [--credential-file <credential-file>] [--key-id <key-id>] [--machine] [--name <name>] [--profile <profile>] [--project <project>] [--quiet] [--region <region>] [--setting <setting>] [--zone <zone>]
```

- `--credential-file`, path: gcp: A service account's credential file, instead of your gcloud login
- `--key-id`, string: aws: The access ID of an AWS credential from the AWS console; its secret is asked for
- `kind`, position 1, string, required: A kind of cloud: aws or gcp
- `--machine`, boolean: gcp: this machine's own service account, from Google's metadata server, with no credential file
- `--name`, string: What to call it [default: its kind]; lets you connect two accounts of one kind
- `--profile`, string: aws: the profile of your aws login to use [default: `AWS_PROFILE`, else default]
- `--project`, string: gcp: the project new things go in [default: --credential-file's, else gcloud's]
- `--quiet`, boolean: Say less, for another of Link's commands running it on the way
- `--region`, string: aws: the region new things go in [default: your aws login's, else us-east-1]
- `--setting`, list of string: Another adapter's own setting, KEY=VALUE, given to it as it is: never a secret, which it asks for
- `--zone`, string: gcp: the zone new machines go in [default: gcloud's, else us-central1-a]

It answers `cloud.listed`.

## `lnk cloud disconnect`

Forget an account and its credential (deletes nothing in it)

```usage
lnk cloud disconnect <name>
```

It takes `name`, position 1, string, required: The account, as `lnk cloud list` names it. It answers `cloud.forgotten`.

## `lnk cloud list`

List the cloud accounts you connected

```usage
lnk cloud list [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It answers `cloud.accounts`.

## `lnk cloud show`

Show a cloud account: its kind, place and who it signs in as, without its credential

```usage
lnk cloud show <name> [--json]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `name`, position 1, string, required: The account, as `lnk cloud list` names it. It answers `cloud.listed`.
